<!-- pr-reviewer: 4f0260f50bd73c9e98e31d6e7c2050eb8c9538b8 -->
Needs changes before merge - and the change requested is evidence, not code. The diff is clean and green on Linux. The Windows crash reproduction that the PR body names as a merge precondition is not present, so the Windows-only crash this fixes cannot be confirmed from this review.

## What looks good

- The six guards land on exactly the tests that make a wgpu device. I checked the split against the code, not just the PR text. The three `tests/egui_app.rs` headless tests reach `headless_gpu::device()` through `shell::headless::run`. The two no-GPU file tests (`a_headless_start_refuses_a_file_it_cannot_open_by_name`, `a_headless_start_with_a_broken_model_fails_by_name`) return from `headless_open::open(cmd)?` before that device call. The three `--ui` refusals return in `lib.rs::run` before `egui_app::run`. So `EGUI_APP_NO_GPU` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu_test_lock.rs:50`) classifies them correctly.
- The new pin `every_headless_run_of_the_egui_app_binary_takes_the_lock` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu_test_lock.rs:69`) parses the current file correctly and would flag a new unguarded test. Both it and the extended `every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock` ran and passed.
- Lock order `gpu_guard()` then `snapshot_guard()` in the three lib snapshot tests matches the existing renderers: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs:234-235` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/review_1710_evidence.rs:79-80`. The guard drops last, so the kittest device drops while the lock is held.
- The guard is not re-entrant and `shell::headless::run` does not take it, so these tests cannot self-deadlock. `test_gpu` also locks, and these tests do not call it while holding the guard.
- Test code only: `#[cfg(test)]` modules plus the integration test, and a decision doc. No process files, no `PROCESS_VERSION`, no `.github` / `.cargo` / `scripts` / `build.rs`, no `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`, no new `camcraft-*` dependency, no snapshot PNG, no golden, no `CHANGELOG.md`. `Process change:` is not needed.
- The decision doc follows the `docs/decisions/README.md` format and names the shared resource, the alternatives dropped, and the limit.
- The body ends `Fixes #3379`, has a `Changelog:` line, and its one commit is a conventional `fix(ui): ...`.

## Results merged with main

Trial merge with current `origin/main` (`c2875fc`): clean, no conflicts. Everything below ran locally on Linux in `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr3972-review`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` | PASS: 11 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (2.7 min) |
| `ui` lib suite | PASS: 1646 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| `ui` egui_app | PASS: 8 passed |
| boundary / boundary_picks / contour_dxf_sketch / sinker_setup / tap_hand / theme_example / theme_files / waterjet_tool | PASS: 3 / 7 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 3 / 17 / 1 |
| both new pins (`every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock`, `every_headless_run_of_the_egui_app_binary_takes_the_lock`) | PASS (ran in the lib suite) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS (clean) |

## Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath change, so no example catalog suite is required for this diff.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): PASS, 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (5.9 min). motion light lib 7 passed; adaptive_troch_island / adaptive_troch_neck / adaptive_troch_parallel 1 each; app pocket_pass_start 1.
- `P2`: no targeted heavy step is owed (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Requested before merge

1. Post the Windows crash reproduction that the PR body names as a precondition: "The M5 coordinator runs the Windows repro on `lenny` and `bacon`. Please wait for that result before the merge, because the merge closes #3379." It is not in the PR and not in #3379, and the decision doc says the crash is not proven (`docs/decisions/3379-ui-gpu-guard.md:30`). Add the result to the PR, or the maintainer waives it in a comment. A Linux review cannot confirm the Windows crash stopped. No code change is requested.

## Questions / notes

- The two pins read source text. They cannot see the crash, and they cannot prove that a test in `EGUI_APP_NO_GPU` makes no device. The decision doc states this limit itself, which is honest.
- The three snapshot tests stay `#[ignore]`d. I did not run the ignored pixel lane for this PR review (AGENTS.md "Pixel snapshots are release-lane"); their guards are confirmed by source inspection only.
- I did not repeat the author's red-before-fix and mutation runs. This diff is outside the safety tier.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4f0260f50bd73c9e98e31d6e7c2050eb8c9538b8 -->
Delta check of the earlier `needs-rework`. That request rested on one missing item: the Windows crash evidence that the PR body names as a precondition.

The evidence is now in the PR. At 05:21Z mkinney posted three runs on the lenny desktop at head `4f0260f50`. Each run took `camcraft-ui --lib` and `--test egui_app` with 12 test threads. All runs passed: 1647 passed and 0 failed for the lib, 8 passed for `egui_app`. No `0xC0000005` and no `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` occurred.

I withdraw the `needs-rework` request. The head did not change since the code review, so its results still hold: quick gate 11 steps with 0 failed, ui lib 1646 passed, `egui_app` 8 passed, light lane 6 of 6 steps, and clippy clean.

Label: `merge-ready`.

One note stays for the maintainer. The crash was intermittent before. This evidence is strong, but it is not a proof. Bacon's check after the merge gives a second Windows machine.
